repairs.value: Strongest feature: Sechler identifies conversation, Christian fellowship, confession, and shared inquiry as goods occasioned by uncertainty, making his reply relevant to Clifton’s challenge and consistent with the precision-and-clarity score of 74. Principal limitation: He contrasts hiddenness with one-hundred-percent certainty, while Clifton questions whether settled awareness of God permits choice, and he never establishes that reflection would disappear rather than acquire different subjects, fitting the evidence-warrant score of 50. Live burden: Sechler needs to explain why divine availability specifically eliminates these investigative goods, and why comparable cooperation could not flourish in a nonhidden world. Locked score: The overall 63 reflects a clear possibility that answers the exchange, tempered by an unproven necessity claim and an overstated contrast.
